LING 101.description: Introduction to the human capacity for language and to how it is acquired. Investigation of language varieties, dialects, and styles. Examination of the social and geographical factors that contribute to language variation and change.
LING 101.subject: LING
LING 101.title: Linguistics 1: Introduction to Language

LING 102.description: Linguistic skills for low-advanced non-native speakers of English related to writing, grammar, reading, listening and speaking for academic purposes. Students enrolled in the International Accelerator Program.
LING 102.subject: LING
LING 102.title: Integrated Linguistic Skills for Non-Native Speakers 1

LING 103.description: Linguistic skills for low-advanced non-native speakers of English related to writing, grammar, reading, listening and speaking for academic purposes with a focus on research skills. Students enrolled in the International Accelerator Program.
LING 103.subject: LING
LING 103.title: Integrated Linguistic Skills for Non-Native Speakers 2

LING 104.description: Linguistic skills for advanced non-native speakers English related to writing, grammar, reading, listening and speaking for academic purposes with a focus on productive skills. Students enrolled in the International Accelerator Program.
LING 104.subject: LING
LING 104.title: Integrated Linguistic Skills for Non-Native Speakers 3

LING 105.description: Topics of a broad nature that require no previous study in linguistics. May be repeated as content varies by title.
LING 105.subject: LING
LING 105.title: Special Topics in Linguistics I

LING 140.description: A course designed to cultivate awareness of phonological and grammatical differences among dialects of English and ability to switch comfortably between one’s dialect and standard usage. Two-hour lecture and laboratory.
LING 140.subject: LING
LING 140.title: Linguistic Diversity Awareness

LING 205.description: Topics of a more focused nature that require no previous study in linguistics. May be repeated as content varies by title.
LING 205.subject: LING
LING 205.title: Special Topics in Linguistics II

LING 232.description: The history of the form and meaning of English words. Coining of words through various processes. The origin of native words and comparison with related languages (German, Dutch, Scandinavian). Borrowing of words from other languages (French, Latin, etc.).
LING 232.subject: LING
LING 232.title: English Word Origins

LING 233.description: Introduction to social scientific concepts and methods for analyzing language and race, drawing primarily on insights from linguistics and anthropology.
LING 233.subject: LING
LING 233.title: Language, Race, and Culture

LING 240.description: Examination of linguistic conflict and rights, as well as centrality of language rights to human rights and personal/cultural identity. Basic facts about language related to identity, culture, attitudes, dialects, bilingualism. Case studies (local, national, international) with particular attention to nationalism, language revitalization, language planning.
LING 240.subject: LING
LING 240.title: Language Conflict and Language Rights

LING 241.description: Linguistic anthropological study of forms of language through the lens of popular culture. Explore the ethnography of communication through play and performance, discursive and semiotic practices, and varieties of language invoked in popular cultural forms that provide resources for cultural reproduction and contestation.
LING 241.subject: LING
LING 241.title: Language and Popular Culture

LING 242.description: Explores language and humor, looking at (i) the linguistic structure and psychology of humor, (ii) changing societal standards for humor, (iii) racial, ethnic, religious, and gender-based humor, and (iv) socio-political questions surrounding the use of these.
LING 242.subject: LING
LING 242.title: Language and Humor at the Intersections of Religion, Race, Ethnicity, and Gender

LING 243.description: Introduction to linguistic and anthropological concepts through the lens of South Korean popular culture.
LING 243.subject: LING
LING 243.title: Korean Popular Culture and Language

LING 244.description: Introduction to basic concepts of sociolinguistics as they apply to the Spanish language.
LING 244.subject: LING
LING 244.title: Spanish Language in Society

LING 273.description: This course introduces students to the fields of interactional sociolinguistics and linguistic anthropology. Students will learn how they approach the study of cross-cultural and intercultural forms of (mis)communication within the context of globally interconnected people, places, and systems of communication.
LING 273.subject: LING
LING 273.title: Cross-Cultural Communication

LING 300.description: Introduction to the linguistic component of human cognition. Properties of speech, the organization of language in the mind/brain, cross-linguistic universals, child language acquisition, and aspects of adult language processing.
LING 300.subject: LING
LING 300.title: Introduction to Language Sciences

LING 301.description: Introduction to the field of linguistics with an emphasis on English. Covers the English sound system, word structure, and grammar. Explores history of English, American dialects, social registers, and style.
LING 301.subject: LING
LING 301.title: The English Language

LING 303.description: A comprehensive and up-to-date survey of Chinese language in a social context, teaching students not only the linguistic structure of modern standard Chinese but also how language and society mutually influence each other in history and today’s digital age. Hands-on instruction to carry out linguistic research.
LING 303.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in CHIN 121.
LING 303.subject: LING
LING 303.title: Chinese Language and Society

LING 305.description: Reading and research on selected topics in linguistics that may require previous study in linguistics or a related field. Prerequisites listed for each course offering. May be repeated as content varies by title.
LING 305.subject: LING
LING 305.title: Special Topics in Linguistics III

LING 310.description: Introduction to syntax and morphology of human language. Exploring basic sentence structure, derived constructions, the structure of the lexicon, and cross-linguistic comparison and generalizations.
LING 310.subject: LING
LING 310.title: Introduction to Syntax and Morphology

LING 311.description: Introduction to speech sounds (phonetics) and their organization and structure in language (phonology). Including vocal tract anatomy, the physical properties of speech, and sound patterns.
LING 311.subject: LING
LING 311.title: The Sounds of Language: Introduction to Phonetics and Phonology

LING 312.description: Introduction to the study of meaning in language, focusing on the core concepts and distinctions between semantics and pragmatics. Includes critical discussion of both theoretical frameworks and real-world examples.
LING 312.subject: LING
LING 312.title: Meaning and Use: Introduction to Semantics and Pragmatics

LING 314.description: Analysis of and practice in pronunciation, listening comprehension, and dialect recognition based on study of the speech sounds, combinations, patterns, and processes of Spanish phonetics and phonology. Department permission required for transfer students.
LING 314.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C+ or better in SPAN 302; placement at 300 level of Phase II placement exam.
LING 314.subject: LING
LING 314.title: Spanish Phonetics and Pronunciation

LING 316.description: Analysis of and practice in pronunciation and listening comprehension.
LING 316.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in both FREN 209 and FREN 210, or equivalents, or a score of F-6 on the French language placement exam.
LING 316.subject: LING
LING 316.title: French Phonetics

LING 340.description: Language in its social setting. The relationship between linguistic categories and culture categories. Language and cognition.
LING 340.subject: LING
LING 340.title: Language, Culture, and Society

LING 345.description: Linguistic examination of the structure, history, and use of language varieties in the U.S., with a particular focus on regional and sociocultural variation and relevant sociolinguistic issues.
LING 345.subject: LING
LING 345.title: Language in the USA

LING 395.description: An intensive, hands-on introduction to principles and techniques of teaching English language learners, exposing students to norms of the field of Teaching English to Speakers of Other Languages (TESOL), working with non-native English speakers, and discovering TESOL opportunities worldwide.
LING 395.subject: LING
LING 395.title: Teaching English Abroad

LING 399.description: Contract approved by instructor, advisor, and program director is required for undergraduate students.
LING 399.subject: LING
LING 399.title: Independent Study

LING 405.description: Intensive study of selected topics; may emphasize interdisciplinary themes.
LING 405.subject: LING
LING 405.title: Topics in Linguistics

LING 421.description: Major structures of English morphology and syntax; role of language history and social and regional variation in understanding contemporary English.
LING 421.subject: LING
LING 421.title: English Grammar

LING 431.description: History of English from the earliest Old English texts through Middle English to Contemporary English. No previous knowledge of Old or Middle English is required.
LING 431.subject: LING
LING 431.title: Development of the English Language

LING 440.description: Patterns in language use as a reflection of social group memberships or the negotiation of interpersonal relationships; special attention to social dialects and stylistic difference in American English.
LING 440.subject: LING
LING 440.title: Language in Society

LING 442.description: Linguistic examination of the structure, history, and use of African-American English, as well as literary presentations, language attitudes, and issues relating to education and the acquisition of Standard English.
LING 442.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: ENGL 101 and ENGL 102, and one course between ENGL 270-ENGL 292.
LING 442.subject: LING
LING 442.title: African-American English

LING 472.description: Acquaints students with principles and practices concerning the use of technology in foreign language teaching. Explores connections between second language acquisition and the implementation of Internet and multimedia technologies.
LING 472.subject: LING
LING 472.title: Introduction to Technology in Language Education

LING 474.description: Bilingual language development, social and cultural aspects of bilingualism, the bilingual brain, bilingualism throughout the lifespan.
LING 474.subject: LING
LING 474.title: Cognitive and Social Aspects of Bilingualism

LING 502.description: The structure, morphology, and syntax of modern French.
LING 502.subject: LING
LING 502.title: French Linguistics

LING 503.description: Structural and descriptive linguistics applied to the German language.
LING 503.subject: LING
LING 503.title: Introduction to German Linguistics

LING 504.description: Phonology, morphology, and syntax of modern Spanish.
LING 504.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in SPAN 303.
LING 504.subject: LING
LING 504.title: Introduction to Spanish Linguistics

LING 505.description: Topics selected by the instructor for specialized study. Course content varies and will be announced in the schedule of classes title. May be repeated with different title.
LING 505.subject: LING
LING 505.title: Interdisciplinary Topics in Linguistics

LING 508.description: An overview of the linguistic structure of Mandarin Chinese through investigation of the phonetics, phonology, morphology, syntax, and lexicon as well as some aspects of sociolinguistics of the language.
LING 508.subject: LING
LING 508.title: Introduction to Chinese Linguistics: Structure of Chinese

LING 512.description: The sound system and its functioning in the morphological system of French from the point of view of current phonological theory.
LING 512.subject: LING
LING 512.title: French Phonology

LING 514.description: Introduction to the study of phonetics and phonology and their application to the sounds and sound systems of English and Spanish. Includes transcription practice and discussion of relevance to teaching.
LING 514.subject: LING
LING 514.title: Contrastive English-Spanish Phonetics and Phonology

LING 521.description: Practical survey of the syntactic structures of English; usage, social and regional variation emphasis on data.
LING 521.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: ENGL 450, LING 421, ENGL 680, or LING 600.
LING 521.subject: LING
LING 521.title: Advanced English Grammar

LING 527.description: Introduction to mathematical mechanisms that play a prominent role in the formalization of syntactic and semantic theories, showing how they are applied to an understanding of the working parts of human language. The topics covered include: set theory, logic, English as a formal language, and languages grammars.
LING 527.subject: LING
LING 527.title: Introduction to Mathematical Methods in Linguistics

LING 530.description: Major ways in which phonetics, phonology, syntax, morphology, and semantics change through language history; social factors which promote innovation.
LING 530.subject: LING
LING 530.title: Language Change

LING 532.description: Coining of words through various processes. Sound and meaning change in the history of words The origin of native words and comparison with related languages (German, Dutch, etc.). Borrowing of words from other languages (French, Latin, etc.). Methodology in etymological research.
LING 532.subject: LING
LING 532.title: English Etymology

LING 533.description: Introduction to historical Germanic linguistics including a survey of the Old Germanic languages (Old English, Old Frisian, Old Saxon, Old High German, Old Norse, Gothic); comparative phonology, morphology, and syntax, typology of modern Germanic languages and dialects; and common Germanic in its Indo-European context.
LING 533.subject: LING
LING 533.title: Introduction to the Germanic Languages

LING 540.description: Introduction to sociolinguistic issues, focusing on a single language. Course content varies and will be announced by title. May be repeated twice as topics vary.
LING 540.subject: LING
LING 540.title: Topics in Language and Culture

LING 541.description: Approaches to gender and language emphasizing the social grounding of both; how language reflects sociocultural values and is a tool for constructing different types of social organization.
LING 541.subject: LING
LING 541.title: Language and Gender

LING 542.description: Research into the parameters governing linguistic conflicts and language rights issues, involving a close examination of the nexes of language and: individual and ethnic identity, culture, dialects, bilingualism. Examination of regional, national, and international case studies, with particular attention to nationalism, language revitalization, and language planning.
LING 542.subject: LING
LING 542.title: Research in Language Conflict and Language Rights

LING 543.description: Anthropological approach to issues of discourse, gender, and emotion. Issues under consideration include the social control, force, and forms of emotional discourse and the relationship between emotion and culture from gender-oriented perspectives.
LING 543.subject: LING
LING 543.title: Discourse, Gender, and Politics of Emotion

LING 545.description: The ways people from various cultures reflect on, reinforce, and construct their social realities through narrating, which will be considered as both artistic expression and social action.
LING 545.subject: LING
LING 545.title: Anthropological Approaches to Narrative and Performance

LING 546.description: Japanese language and communication in its socio-cultural context; emphasis on comparison with American English. Taught in English.
LING 546.subject: LING
LING 546.title: Japanese Language in Society

LING 548.description: Introduction to the study of variation in Modern German. Traditional German dialectology and dialect geography, language and society, multilingualism in the German-speaking countries, German in contact with other languages.
LING 548.subject: LING
LING 548.title: German Sociolinguistics

LING 554.description: Description of the grammatical structures of Modern Spanish. Intensive study of the theory and practice of word formation and sentence structure of Spanish.
LING 554.subject: LING
LING 554.title: The Structure of Modern Spanish

LING 556.description: Anthropological approach to issues of language and globalization. Linguistic consequences of globalization under consideration include communicative patterns, linguistic change, and language and political economy.
LING 556.subject: LING
LING 556.title: Language and Globalization

LING 565.description: An examination of concepts and problems such as meaning, reference, analyticity, definition, and the relation between logic and philosophy.
LING 565.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or higher in PHIL 114 or PHIL 511.
LING 565.subject: LING
LING 565.title: Philosophy of Language

LING 567.description: Theories of speech perception, linguistic theories of syntax and semantics, the brain mechanisms underlying language, the development of language in children, and the role of language in thought.
LING 567.subject: LING
LING 567.title: Psychology of Language

LING 570.description: The language acquisition process in normal children, including the development of semantics, morphology, syntax, phonology, and pragmatics; American dialects and bilingualism.
LING 570.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in COMD 501 and C or better in COMD 507.
LING 570.subject: LING
LING 570.title: Introduction to Language Development

LING 600.description: Survey of core areas of linguistics and extensions to closely related disciplines. Introduction to the linguistic component of human cognition. Formal description and analysis of the general properties of speech and language, the organization of language in the mind/brain, and cross-linguistic typology and universals.
LING 600.subject: LING
LING 600.title: Survey of Linguistics

LING 627.description: Introduction to the study of linguistic meaning, including the following topics: meaning, reference, and truth; the connections among language, thought, and reality; word meaning and sentence meaning; possible worlds and modality; thematic roles; meaning and context; presupposition and implicature; speech acts; formal semantics; and cognitive semantics.
LING 627.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in any of LING 300, LING 301, LING 600, PHIL 114, PHIL 511.
LING 627.subject: LING
LING 627.title: Introduction to Semantics and Pragmatics

LING 650.description: Foundations of generative morphology, focusing on morphological data collection and analysis; the structure of the lexicon; and the interfaces between morphology and phonology, semantics, and syntax.
LING 650.subject: LING
LING 650.title: Introduction to Morphology

LING 701.description: Description, visualization, and basic statistical analysis of both discrete and continuous linguistic data from various linguistic subfields using R.
LING 701.subject: LING
LING 701.title: Quantitative Approaches to Linguistic Analysis

LING 702.description: Addresses a range of methodological and professional issues potentially encountered when conducting research in linguistics.
LING 702.subject: LING
LING 702.title: Research Methods in Linguistics

LING 710.description: The phonetic basis of phonology; phonological structure; lexical representation; cross-linguistic survey of major types of phonological processes; emphasis on data analysis.
LING 710.subject: LING
LING 710.title: Introduction to Phonology

LING 711.description: Advanced study of theoretical issues in phonology.
LING 711.subject: LING
LING 711.title: Phonological Theory

LING 712.description: Physical and anatomical mechanisms for producing speech, phonetic representations and models of speech perception and prosody, acoustic characteristics of the speech signal, use of international phonetic alphabet symbols (IPA) to describe speech sounds in the world's languages, training in experimental and field methods in phonetic research.
LING 712.subject: LING
LING 712.title: Articulatory and Acoustic Phonetics

LING 720.description: Foundations of generative grammar, focusing on the syntax of English; universal principles of basic clause structure and derived constructions; emphasis on syntactic argumentation and cross- linguistic generalization.
LING 720.subject: LING
LING 720.title: Introduction to Syntax

LING 721.description: Advanced exploration of a principled model of the syntactic component of universal grammar and the interface between this module and semantic interpretations and lexical information. Competing hypotheses are compared.
LING 721.subject: LING
LING 721.title: Syntactic Theory

LING 728.description: The formal study of linguistic meaning, including the following topics: Fregean truth-conditional semantics; lexical decomposition; predication and modification; lambda abstraction; generalized quantification; intentional and extensional contexts; tense, aspect, and modality; propositional attitudes; and indexicality.
LING 728.subject: LING
LING 728.title: Semantic Theory

LING 729.description: Study of formal approaches to pragmatic phenomena such as focus, presupposition, and implicature; examination of deictic, contextual and perspectival expressions; survey of pragmatic frameworks such as Relevance Theory and Discourse Representation Theory; study of information structural properties of natural languages, including topic- comment structure, given-new contrasts, definiteness versus indefiniteness.
LING 729.subject: LING
LING 729.title: Pragmatic Theory

LING 730.description: Innovation in phonology, morphology, syntax, and semantics; evidence from texts, social and regional dialects; emphasis on theories of language change.
LING 730.subject: LING
LING 730.title: Historical Linguistics

LING 731.description: The historical background of Modern English with attention to the major linguistic and cultural developments which distinguish English from other related languages. No prior knowledge of Old English or Middle English is required.
LING 731.subject: LING
LING 731.title: History of English Language

LING 732.description: Development of the French language from its origins to 1600.
LING 732.subject: LING
LING 732.title: History of the French Language

LING 733.description: Development of German in the Germanic, Old High German, Middle High German, and New High German periods. Phonology, morphology, syntax, semantics, and the relationship between dialects and the standard language.
LING 733.subject: LING
LING 733.title: History of the German Language

LING 734.description: Development of the language from its origins to the present day.
LING 734.subject: LING
LING 734.title: History of the Spanish Language

LING 739.description: Introduces basic resources of discipline and focuses on the development of linguistics in terms of dominant issues and analytical methodology with emphasis on paradigm shifts.
LING 739.subject: LING
LING 739.title: The Evolution of Linguistic Theory, Practice, and Methods

LING 740.description: An examination of choices speakers in the same community make between styles, dialects, and languages; their association with social group memberships; speakers’ perceptions of interpersonal relationships.
LING 740.subject: LING
LING 740.title: Introduction to Sociolinguistics

LING 741.description: Linguistic approaches to the history, structure, and use of African American English.
LING 741.subject: LING
LING 741.title: African American English

LING 742.description: Sociolinguistic examination of the relationship between language and race, including ethnolects, identity construction, linguistic appropriation, linguistic racism, and antiracism in everyday and institutional contexts.
LING 742.subject: LING
LING 742.title: Language and Race

LING 743.description: Types of interactive organization found within conversation and the methods and procedures used by participants to achieve order.
LING 743.subject: LING
LING 743.title: Analysis of Conversation

LING 744.description: The structural effects of contact between speakers of more than one language on the language involved. Borrowing, code-switching, convergence, language death, development of pidgins and creoles.
LING 744.subject: LING
LING 744.title: Language Contact Phenomena

LING 745.description: Social and regional variation in American English since the colonial period.
LING 745.subject: LING
LING 745.title: Varieties of American English

LING 746.description: The intersection between variation in phonetic/phonological form and social factors (such as a speaker’s region, age, group identity, ethnic background, sexual orientation, level of education, etc.), acoustic production of variation, effects of sociophonetic variation on speech perception, on language change, and on language acquisition.
LING 746.subject: LING
LING 746.title: Sociophonetics

LING 747.description: Examines language as a social, cultural, and political matrix. Topics include ideology, gender, race, power, agency, and resistance. Students will apply linguistic theories in their own analyses of everyday speech.
LING 747.subject: LING
LING 747.title: Language as Social Action

LING 748.description: A comprehensive introduction to linguistic anthropology, its relationship(s) to sociolinguistics, discourse analysis, and conversation analysis. Contributions made to social theory and theories of language and discourse will be understood.
LING 748.subject: LING
LING 748.title: Introduction to Linguistic Anthropology

LING 749.description: A theoretical and practical graduate introduction to variationist sociolinguistics. The theoretical portion of the course will center on foundational concepts for the study of variation, while the practical portion involves an introduction to quantitative data analysis and sociolinguistic data collection.
LING 749.subject: LING
LING 749.title: Sociolinguistic Variation

LING 765.description: Examination of concepts such as meaning, reference, analyticity, and translational indeterminacy; evaluation of accounts of speech acts, the semantics of propositional attitudes, and metaphor and other pragmatic phenomena.
LING 765.subject: LING
LING 765.title: Studies in Philosophy of Language

LING 772.description: Introduction to technology in language teaching and the connection between language acquisition and the implementation of Internet and multimedia technology.
LING 772.subject: LING
LING 772.title: Technology in Foreign Language Education

LING 780.description: Underlying principles of how phonological, syntactic, and lexical features are organized above the sentence level; alternative choices of these features and how they contribute to the speaker’s/writer’s goals.
LING 780.subject: LING
LING 780.title: Discourse Analysis

LING 782.description: Linguistic anthropological approaches that examine how ideological systems mediate social structures and Iinguistic /discursive forms and functions. Topics range from language and political economy, identity and identifications, institutions, and nation-building/nationalism.
LING 782.subject: LING
LING 782.title: Language Ideology: The Political Economy of Language Beliefs and Practices

LING 790.description: Study of current theory and research in second language acquisition and exploration of relationships between such work and classroom second language learning and teaching. Examination of research techniques used in applied linguistics.
LING 790.subject: LING
LING 790.title: Second Language Acquisition

LING 791.description: Current issues and research in adult second language acquisition, with special attention to developments in theory and to methodological issues and considerations.
LING 791.subject: LING
LING 791.title: Theory and Methodology in Second Language Acquisition

LING 792.description: An analysis of instructed second language acquisition (SLA). This course explores the historical development and up-to-date findings in foreign/second language research and applies that knowledge to classroom teaching methods. Students will be expected to conduct empirical investigation.
LING 792.subject: LING
LING 792.title: Principles of Instructed Second Language Acquisition and Foreign Language Teaching

LING 794.description: An exploration of the most important and fascinating aspects of individual and societal bilingualism, focusing on both theoretical and practical issues.
LING 794.subject: LING
LING 794.title: Bilingualism

LING 795.description: Survey of teaching ESOL, including theoretical principles and practical strategies for approaches, methods, techniques, and materials as they concern elementary, secondary, and postsecondary learners.
LING 795.subject: LING
LING 795.title: Principles and Strategies for Teaching ESOL

LING 796.description: This course surveys research on the mental processes and linguistic contexts involved in reading and writing in a second language. Pedagogical implications for elementary, secondary, and postsecondary learners are discussed.
LING 796.subject: LING
LING 796.title: Teaching Reading and Writing to ESOL Learners: Theory and Practice

LING 798.description: Observation and supervised teaching of English to speakers of other languages in an individually designed classroom setting. Course may be taken up to 3 times.
LING 798.subject: LING
LING 798.title: Practicum in Teaching ESOL

LING 805.description: Topics selected by the instructor for specialized study. May be repeated as topics vary.
LING 805.subject: LING
LING 805.title: Topics in Linguistics

LING 820.description: Advanced exploration in syntactic theory, involving either cross-theoretical examination of specific linguistic phenomena or in-depth study of a particular theoretical model.
LING 820.subject: LING
LING 820.title: Seminar in Syntax

LING 830.description: Special topics in historical and comparative linguistics, such as historical phonology or syntax, Indo-European linguistics, and comparative Germanic or Romance linguistics.
LING 830.subject: LING
LING 830.title: Seminar in Historical Linguistics

LING 840.description: Current theories relevant to specialized consideration of the social functions of linguistic choices at any level of analysis; variation as a reflection of region and social group membership or interpersonal relationships.
LING 840.subject: LING
LING 840.title: Seminar in Language Variation

LING 890.description: Special topics in the acquisition of language such as first language acquisition of English or other languages, cross-linguistic effects on acquisition, or issues in acquisition theory.
LING 890.subject: LING
LING 890.title: Seminar in Language Acquisition

LING 891.description: Special topics in teaching English to speakers of other languages (ESOL), such as materials design, program design and evaluation, or teaching a particular language skill.
LING 891.subject: LING
LING 891.title: Seminar in English for Speakers of Other Languages (ESOL)
